subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix prioritize pi-tui renderer behavior, OpenClaw-owned viewport/follow state, or an explicit TUI auto-scroll preference?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the permanent fix affects terminal UX policy and dependency ownership rather than being a narrow code-only repair.

options.title: Fix renderer and anchor behavior
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback while following only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll preference
options.body: Expose explicit terminal follow behavior, accepting a new settings surface and fresh/upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Hold for live repro only
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a current-main PTY capture demonstrates the exact jump and renderer reason.

recommendation.title: Fix renderer and anchor behavior
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback while following only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: They already handled adjacent auto-scroll product behavior and explicitly separated the browser fix from this TUI issue.
